extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of literary criticism; readers/distributors of Project Gutenberg eBooks
extracted.subtask_description: An academic critical-biographical essay on the Marquis d'Argenson that also includes paratext (transcriber's note) and the full Project Gutenberg license; contains guidance on how to approach literary/character criticism and explicit legal/operational rules for distributing the eBook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critic's temper: proceed patiently and tenderly
rubrics_metrics.description: When the critic deals with material that is 'new and unessayed' or a man of delicate fabric, 'the critic will proceed very patiently and tenderly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid resorting to accredited methods or hasty generalisations; watch the 'texture of the clay' and let the subject's particularities guide treatment rather than imposing standard formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid presenting subject by prevailing prejudice or provincial opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic 'will beware of presenting him, morally or otherwise, in the light of the prevailing prejudice; nor will he erect his own provincialities of opinion as a final measure of wisdom or worth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not moralise or evaluate the subject according to contemporary popular biases; refrain from treating the critic's own views as the definitive standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let the subject tell his own tale; emphasise understanding over judging
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather will the critic 'let the man go his own way and tell his own tale, content if he may but follow and hear and understand, without sitting in the gate to judge him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise empathetic reconstruction and careful listening to evidence over immediate verdicts; adopt a descriptive/interpretive stance before moral judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek the 'secret' of singularities; avoid haste and impatience
rubrics_metrics.description: Without knowledge of the secret causes of a subject's singularities of temper, critics are apt to 'yield to that haste and impatience which they are too often apt to provoke.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate formative influences and hidden motives; once these are understood, reserve irritation and instead combine pity for weaknesses with admiration for virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use family/portraits/ancestry and small archival traces to inform character study
rubrics_metrics.description: When puzzled by a character of the past 'a saunter in the portrait gallery of the old house is often pregnant with suggestion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ biographical/contextual sources (portraits, family history, archives) as legitimate evidence to illuminate temperament and background when other resources fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual knowledge of upbringing and milieu is essential for just criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: In default of knowledge of 'the man and his mind' and the influences that shaped him, 'it is impossible to criticise his life with justice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather and incorporate evidence about upbringing, social environment, education and formative events before forming final assessments of a historical subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style as evidence of character: 'Le style, c'est l'homme.'
rubrics_metrics.description: The table of contents highlights the theme 'Le style, c'est l'homme' (style is the man), implying that stylistic features reveal personal character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stylistic analysis of writing as a critical tool to infer aspects of personality, temperament and disposition; stylistic traits are substantive biographical evidence.
